title: Stage 1: Reading a scenario
summary: Turn a text description of a TLS setup into real certificates and an X509Chain result.

steps.title: What you are building
body: Most certificate tickets come down to six problems: a missing intermediate, an untrusted root, an expired certificate, a name mismatch, the wrong EKU, or a chain in the wrong order. **chain-doctor** diagnoses them.

It reads a **scenario** from stdin that describes what a server sends and what the client trusts, builds real certificates to match (a fixed `CN=Doctor Root` and `CN=Doctor Issuing CA`, both valid 2020 to 2050, and a leaf), runs `X509Chain` at **2030-06-01**, and, by the last stage, prints a diagnosis with the command that confirms it and the command that fixes it.
| `host NAME` | the name the client connects to (required) |
| `names A B ...` | DNS names in the leaf's SAN; the first is also its CN (default: the host) |
| `sends leaf intermediate root` | what the server sends, in order (`leaf` required) |
| `trusts root` / `trusts nothing` | the client's trust store (default: nothing) |
Parse the scenario, build the leaf, and print a summary plus the raw chain result:

steps.prompt: A scenario says `sends leaf` and `trusts root`. Which two `X509Chain` settings model that?
options: Only the leaf is built; the root goes in `CustomTrustStore` and `ExtraStore` stays empty
The root goes in `ExtraStore` and the leaf in `CustomTrustStore`
Neither: `X509Chain` always uses the machine store
steps.explain: `ExtraStore` is what the server sent beyond the leaf. `CustomTrustStore` (with `CustomRootTrust`) is the client's trust anchors. Nothing else is available, because downloads are disabled.

steps.prompt: Match each scenario line to what your code does with it.
The server forgot its intermediate. What does this print?
code: var root = DojoCert("CN=Doctor Root", null, true, nbYear: 2020, naYear: 2050);
var inter = DojoCert("CN=Doctor Issuing CA", root, true, nbYear: 2020, naYear: 2050);
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
steps.explain: Without the intermediate nothing links the leaf to the root: `PartialChain`. Hand it the intermediate, as a good server does, and the same chain builds.

steps.title: chain-doctor: parse and build
prompt: | `host NAME` | the name the client connects to (required) |
| `names A B ...` | DNS names in the leaf's SAN; the first is also its CN (default: the host) |
| `sends leaf intermediate root` | what the server sends, in order (`leaf` required) |
| `trusts root` / `trusts nothing` | the client's trust store (default: nothing) |
Skip blank lines and `#` comments. Report problems with the scenario itself and stop with `return -1` (but keep printing `error:` lines for unknown lines and carry on):
- no `leaf` in `sends`: `error: the server must send a leaf` (stop)
- anything other than `leaf`, `intermediate`, `root` in `sends`: `error: unknown certificate 'X'` (stop)

The leaf: `CN=` + first name, SAN with every name, not a CA, `DigitalSignature`, EKU serverAuth, SKI, AKI, signed by `inter`, valid 2030-01-01 to 2031-01-01 (the `isExpired` and `usage` parameters come into play later; ignore them for now or handle them already).
server sends: SUBJECTS IN THE ORDER SENT
chain: valid                    (or: chain: FLAG, FLAG sorted by name)
Build with `CustomRootTrust`, serverAuth application policy, `NoCheck` revocation, downloads disabled, `VerificationTime = at`.
starter: var inter = MakeCa("CN=Doctor Issuing CA", root);
// parse host / names / sends / trusts, build the leaf, print the summary and the chain line
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, Day(2020), Day(2050), new byte[] { 0x10, 0x01 });
X509Certificate2 MakeLeaf(string[] dns, bool isExpired, string usage)
// CN = dns[0], SAN = every name, EKU from usage, signed by inter
static DateTimeOffset Day(int year) => new DateTimeOffset(year, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
solution: var inter = MakeCa("CN=Doctor Issuing CA", root);
if (host == "") { Console.WriteLine("error: no host line"); return -1; }
if (!sends.Contains("leaf")) { Console.WriteLine("error: the server must send a leaf"); return -1; }
var bad = sends.FirstOrDefault(s => s != "leaf" && s != "intermediate" && s != "root");
if (bad != null) { Console.WriteLine($"error: unknown certificate '{bad}'"); return -1; }
if (names == null || names.Length == 0) names = new[] { host };
var byName = new Dictionary<string, X509Certificate2> { ["leaf"] = leaf, ["intermediate"] = inter, ["root"] = root };
var flags = chain.ChainStatus.Select(s => s.Status).Where(f => f != X509ChainStatusFlags.NoError)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, Day(2020), Day(2050), new byte[] { 0x10, 0x01 });
X509Certificate2 MakeLeaf(string[] dns, bool isExpired, string usage)
var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=" + dns[0], key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(oid) }, false));
return req.Create(inter, Day(isExpired ? 2028 : 2030), Day(isExpired ? 2029 : 2031), new byte[] { 0x20, 0x01 });
static DateTimeOffset Day(int year) => new DateTimeOffset(year, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
hints: `var words = line.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);` then `switch (words[0])`. `words[1..]` gives the rest.
Map tokens to certificates: `new Dictionary<string, X509Certificate2> { ["leaf"] = leaf, ["intermediate"] = inter, ["root"] = root }`.
